# tools/dist — deterministic dist pipeline

This directory builds every binary that ships in the gitd deployment:

- **image binaries** (static, musl, built in an Alpine chroot):
  `openssh`, `git`, `fish`, `ca-certificates`
- **host binaries** (static, glibc, built in an AL2023 chroot):
  `containerd`, `runc`
- **toolchain**: the pinned Go SDK (`build-pinned-go.sh`)

Every artifact is a deterministic static-binary tarball published to
`ChronicCmposer/gitd` GitHub Releases — the PRIMARY gitd repo, under stable
**family release tags** (`openssh-dist`, `git-dist`, `fish-dist`,
`ca-certs-dist`, `containerd-dist`, `runc-dist`; strimserver
family-tag strategy, R3-Q2) — and mirrored to `s3://git.cmposer.cc`
(fallback). Bazel consumes the tarballs through the checksummed repo rules in
`//:dist.bzl`, whose sha256 pins are generated by `gen-dist-pins.sh` and
committed in `//:dist_pins.bzl`.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `versions.sh` | single source of truth for every pin (version, URL, sha256) |
| `lib.sh` | shared fail-fast helpers (die, downloads, deterministic tarball) |
| `chroot.sh` | alpine (musl) + AL2023 (glibc) chroot setup, content-addressed cache under `~/.cache/gitd-dist` |
| `build-openssh.sh` | static OpenSSH 10.5p1, OpenSSL-linked, auth-identity patch, seccomp sandbox |
| `build-git.sh` | minimal static git 2.53.0 (NO_PERL/NO_GETTEXT/.../NO_OPENSSL) |
| `build-fish.sh` | static fish 4.9.3 (cmake + rust, system pcre2-static) |
| `build-ca-certs.sh` | pinned Alpine ca-certificates -> `/etc/ssl/certs` trust store |
| `build-containerd.sh` | containerd 2.3.5 host binary (AL2023 chroot, CGO_ENABLED=0, no seccomp tag) |
| `build-runc.sh` | runc 1.2.9 host binary (same rules) |
| `build-pinned-go.sh` | pinned Go 1.26.5 toolchain (aligned with rules_go 0.63.0) |
| `check-dist.sh` | build-twice determinism check (byte-identical tarballs) |
| `gen-dist-pins.sh` | regenerate `//:dist_pins.bzl` sha256 pins from built tarballs |
| `publish-dist.sh` | publish a checked artifact to GitHub Releases + S3 |
| `patches/` | OpenSSH auth-identity patch (R2-Q6 Option A) |
| `containerd/` | systemd unit + config.toml installed on the host (R2-Q19) |
| `out/` | built artifacts (gitignored) |

## Workflow

```sh
# 1. Build every product and prove determinism (build twice, compare sha256).
make check-openssh-dist check-git-dist check-fish-dist \
     check-ca-certs-dist check-containerd-dist check-runc-dist check-pinned-go-dist

# 2. Regenerate the Bazel pins from the verified tarballs and commit.
make gen-dist-pins

# 3. Publish to GitHub Releases (primary) + S3 (fallback).
make publish-openssh-dist publish-git-dist ...
```

`publish-dist.sh` **GPG-signs** each artifact before upload (detached
ASCII-armored `.asc`, operator key via `GPG_KEY_ID`) and uploads the `.asc`
alongside the tarball on both channels, so consumers can prove provenance
against the committed public key `tools/release/gitd-signing-key.asc`
(fail-fast if signing fails — no unsigned dist product is ever published).

Requirements: root, passwordless sudo, **or** working unprivileged user
namespaces (non-root chroot builds), network, `curl`, `tar`, `unshare`
(util-linux), `openssl` (ca-certificates), an authenticated `gh` CLI
(`gh auth login`) and `aws` CLI (publish only).

The alpine and AL2023 chroots are cached in the **home directory** — never
`/tmp` and never the repo — under
`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/gitd-dist/rootfs-<flavor>-<arch>-<id>/`.
The cache dir name is content-addressed: `<id>` is the sha256 of a
deterministic fingerprint of every build-determining input (flavor, build
arch, the pinned `versions.sh`, the rootfs base, and the requesting product's
sorted apk/dnf dependency set), so a dependency change gets a NEW dir
automatically and two products with identical deps share one rootfs.
Provisioning is atomic (`.provisioned` sentinel written into `$rootfs.new`
before the `mv` into place), so an aborted build resumes cleanly; delete
`~/.cache/gitd-dist` to force a fresh base.

## Non-root builds (user namespaces)

The chroot builds need uid-0 semantics. The privilege wrapper in `chroot.sh`
(`ns_enter`, mirroring the strimserver reference harness) tries, in order:
real root (private mount+pid namespace), passwordless sudo (`sudo -n`), and
finally a fresh user namespace via `unshare -Urmpf` (user + map-root-user +
mount + pid + fork). A non-root user with working userns never needs sudo or
root; when none of the three works the pipeline fails loudly with the exact
remediation.

The rootfs tarballs ship char device nodes under `/dev/` (e.g. AL2023's
`/dev/null` as `1,3`); `mknod` of char/block devices needs `CAP_MKNOD` in the
*initial* user namespace, which an unprivileged userns does not grant. So
extraction skips the whole `/dev` tree (`--exclude='dev/*'`,
`--no-same-owner`) and the host device nodes are bind-mounted into the chroot
at run time, together with `proc` (`sysfs` is not mountable in an
unprivileged userns on most kernels and is not needed for these static
builds). The whole sequence — extract → create `dev`/`proc`/`sys` →
bind-mount → `chroot` → build — runs under a single `unshare` invocation (see
`ns_enter` in `chroot.sh`); the uid/gid mapping is fixed at namespace
creation and the mount/chroot capabilities only exist inside that same
namespace.

On hosts where the kernel blocks unprivileged user namespaces
(`kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0`, `user.max_user_namespaces=0`, or
AppArmor's `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`), run the build as real
root (or with passwordless sudo) — the pipeline then uses a private mount+pid
namespace directly (same bind-mount logic, no `--user`).
`make check-openssh-dist-deps` verifies the root-or-sudo-or-userns
precondition up front. Note the cached rootfs keeps the archive's read-only
directory modes, so a non-root operator who needs to force a rebuild may have
to `chmod -R u+w` before removing a `~/.cache/gitd-dist/rootfs-*` dir.

## Determinism (2.3)

Each `build-*.sh` pins:

- `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (fixed in `versions.sh`) — passed to tar/gzip so no
  build timestamp leaks into the artifact;
- the exact product version and (where available) upstream sha256;
- `--sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --group=0` for the
  tarball, and `gzip -n` to drop the gzip header timestamp.

`make check-<product>-dist` runs the build twice into separate directories and
compares sha256 of every output; a mismatch fails loudly and blocks publish.

## Auth-identity patch

`patches/openssh-10.5p1-auth-identity.patch` (R2-Q6 Option A) teaches
`session.c:do_setup_env` to export `SSH_AUTH_KEY_FP`, `SSH_AUTH_KEY_TYPE`, and
`SSH_AUTH_CERT_ID` from the authenticated key into the forced-command child
environment. gitd reads these in every git session (R10-Q5: missing vars fail
closed). The patch is applied by `build-openssh.sh`; `patch -p1` applies it
cleanly to the pristine 10.5p1 tree.

## S3 prefix layout (2.4)

Bucket `git.cmposer.cc`, region `us-east-2`:

| Prefix | Artifacts |
|--------|-----------|
| `openssh/` | `openssh-10.5p1.linux-<arch>.tar.gz` |
| `git/` | `git-2.53.0.linux-<arch>.tar.gz` |
| `fish/` | `fish-4.9.3.linux-<arch>.tar.gz` |
| `ca-certs/` | `ca-certificates-20260611-r0.linux-<arch>.tar.gz` |
| `containerd/` | `containerd-2.3.5.linux-<arch>.tar.gz`, `runc-1.2.9.linux-<arch>.tar.gz` |
| `image/` | `gitd-container.tar` (rules_oci image tarball, published to the `gitd-container` family release tag) |

Every artifact above is published with its detached GPG signature
(`<artifact>.asc`) in the same prefix / release.

GitHub family release tags on `ChronicCmposer/gitd` (strimserver family-tag
strategy: one stable tag per product, assets clobber-uploaded on every pin
bump): `openssh-dist`, `git-dist`, `fish-dist`, `ca-certs-dist`,
`containerd-dist`, `runc-dist`, plus `gitd-container` for
the container image. Bazel repo rules (`//:dist.bzl`) try GitHub first, then
S3; both URLs must match the pinned sha256.

## Bazel integration

- `//:dist.bzl` declares `@openssh_dist_<arch>`, `@git_dist_<arch>`,
  `@fish_dist_<arch>`, `@ca_certs_dist_<arch>`,
  `@containerd_dist_<arch>`, `@runc_dist_<arch>` via `http_archive` with the
  pins from `//:dist_pins.bzl`.
- `//image:image` (rules_oci `oci_image`, `tags = ["manual"]`) assembles the
  from-scratch image from those tarballs + the in-repo `image/fs` files.
  Because the image needs the published dist tarballs, it is excluded from
  the default `//...` build; build it explicitly after publishing artifacts.

## Out of scope here

Building the chroots needs root, passwordless sudo, **or** unprivileged user
namespaces and network; the sandboxed CI can syntax check and shellcheck the
scripts, and `make check-ca-certs-dist` runs rootless (it only needs
openssl). Actual openssh/git/fish/containerd/runc builds must run on the
real build host (or a host with unprivileged userns enabled).
